manifestations.description: A patch of devitalised skin at lateral and lower aspect of right thigh.
abrasion lateral surface of right leg with laceration wound over medial malleolus.
Pain and limitation of movement left shoulder.
restriction on the knee joint movement.
As a result of the fractured femur, her right leg is ½ inch shorter than the left.
a skin graft on the antero lateral aspect of the thigh close to the knee causing a 3" diameter smooth brown scar.
the removal of the skin therefrom left a scar 2½" x 6". This scar was described as being flat but with some raised brown streaks.
the scars are not ugly but sufficiently noticeable for the plaintiff to be reluctant to reveal them, say, by wearing a bathing suit or shorts or similar summer attire.
The knee joint impairment has not improved and will not improve.
The scars resulting from the grafts have not improved and, will not improve and the cosmetic impairment is now 2%.

treatments_received: a split skin graft was done on 12th March 1982 for the devitalised skin on the right thigh.
the fracture of the shaft of the femur was treated conservatively with skeletal traction, then a long leg cylinder and cast brace.
the fracture of the clavicle was treated conservatively with a figure of 8 bandage.
rehabilitation physiotherapy treatment in the phsiotherapy department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital.

losses.description: Shortening of the right leg and impairment of the movement of the knee.
3" diameter smooth brown scar on anterolateral thigh and donor scar 2½" x 6"; scars are sufficiently noticeable causing reluctance to reveal them by wearing a bathing suit or shorts.
